preamble: Fricativization of the palatal lateral [ʎ] to the voiced postalveolar fricative [ʒ]: the lateral release is lost and the sound becomes a central sibilant fricative. In early Castilian the /ʎ/ that came from Vulgar Latin -lj-, -cl- and -gl- became /ʒ/ (fīlius > Old Spanish fijo /ˈhiʒo/, oclus > ojo /ˈoʒo/), while Portuguese keeps /ʎ/ (filho, olho). Castilian /ʒ/ was later devoiced to /ʃ/ and then backed to /x/, giving Modern Spanish hijo, ojo and mujer.

examples.from: Latin fīlius 'son', with -lj- > /ʎ/ (Portuguese filho keeps it)
Vulgar Latin oclus 'eye' (Classical oculus), with -cl- > /ʎ/ (Portuguese olho keeps it)

examples.note: Only this early /ʎ/ became /ʒ/. The /ʎ/ that Castilian later developed from Latin -ll- and from initial pl-, cl-, fl- stayed a lateral (caballo, llamar < clamare).

sources: Wikipedia contributors (2026). History of the Spanish language. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_Spanish_language
